data.gender_notes: Anthe is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Anthe represents the goddess of breath, blowing tenderly on new life. In Christianity, Anthe symbolizes the breath of the Holy Spirit bestowed upon believers. The name Anthe carries the meaning “Graceful breath” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Anthe usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful breath and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of God's grace and breath of life
data.etymology: Anthe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful breath.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anthe total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: אנתה
in_hebrew.meaning: פרח, צמח, או קורטוב של שמחה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם 'אנתה' מקורו כנראה מהמילה היוונית 'ἄνθος' (אנתוס), שפירושה 'פרח'. במסגרת השמות הנוצריים, 'אנתה' עשוי להיות קשור למושגים של צמיחה, שמחה, ותקווה, כפי שמתבטא בכתבי הקודש ובמסורות הנוצריות. השם עשוי לשקף את היופי והחיות שבפרח, ועל כן הוא עשוי להיות מיועד לנערות שגדלות באהבה ובאור.

in_greek.name: Άνθη
in_greek.meaning: Άνθος, το λουλούδι, ή η ανθοφορία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα 'Άνθη' προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'ἄνθος' (anthos), που σημαίνει 'flower'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη και στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία, τα άνθη συχνά συμβόλιζαν την πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την αιώνια ζωή. Το όνομα 'Άνθη' μπορεί να αντανακλά την ιδέα της πνευματικής αναγέννησης και της ελπίδας για το μέλλον, όπως εκφράζεται στις Παιδαγωγικές και στις λειτουργικές παραδόσεις της Ορθόδοξης Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Anthe
in_latin.meaning: Flos, floris; vel, brevis gaudii indicium
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen 'Anthe' originem trahit ex voce Graeca 'ἄνθος' (anthos), quae 'florem' significat. In ecclesia primitiva et in traditione christiana, flos saepe vitam aeternam et spem resurrectionis indicabat. Nomen 'Anthe' potest significare gaudium, spem, et pulchritudinem, quae in floribus expressa sunt, et in Scripturis et in liturgia christiana occurrunt.

in_english.name: Anthe
in_english.meaning: A flower; symbolizing growth, joy, and eternal life
in_english.long_meaning: The name 'Anthe' originates from the Greek word 'ἄνθος' (anthos), meaning 'flower'. In Christian tradition, flowers often symbolize spiritual growth, joy, and the promise of eternal life. The name 'Anthe' may reflect these themes, suggesting a person characterized by hope, beauty, and spiritual vitality. Historically, flowers have been used in Christian liturgy and iconography to represent purity, love, and devotion. Today, 'Anthe' is used across various Christian cultures to signify a connection to these values.

data.cultural_impact: Anthe holds a rich cultural history, derived from the ancient Greek mythology where Anthe is the goddess of breath or blowing tenderly. It is believed that she breathes life into newborn babies by gently blowing them with her breath.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Anthe holds a deeper spiritual significance as it symbolizes the breath of the Holy Spirit being bestowed upon believers. The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Christian Trinity and is believed to be present in the creation, guidance, and empowerment of humans. In the biblical account of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit descended upon the followers of Jesus Christ in the form of tongues of flames. This event is commonly known as the "birthday of the Church," as it marked the beginning of the Christian mission to spread the gospel around the world. Anthe serves as a reminder of the divine presence that breathes new life and strength into the believers on their spiritual journey.
